correctness.rationale: At each internal vertex, image-cone equality characterizes bounded morphisms. Child-root choices for middle labels yield Q=product(1+q_i); inclusion–exclusion for root bottom counts Z=product(N_i)-2Q+1. Hence N=Z+2Q+1=product(N_i)+2, with N(leaf)=1. The integer-partition envelope F(k) has weights 1,3,5 on sizes 1,2,3 and unique maximizing composition into twos and at most one three; its supermultiplicativity and F(k)>2+F(k-1) for k>=4 bound every tree. The specific roots with two- and three-vertex chain children meet the bound; equality analysis yields uniqueness. The minimum follows from all child factors >=1 and equality iff all children are leaves. The standalone independent direct checker enumerates the exact back condition for every unlabelled rooted-tree shape through size seven and independently compares the recurrence; it checks extremality for shapes through size ten. All hypotheses and n=1,2,3,4 exceptional cases are explicitly handled.

originality.rationale: The claim of novelty is limited to the all-order sharp extremum and unique rooted-tree extremizers of the complete (not necessarily surjective) diamond bounded-morphism count. A directly overlapping earlier result already provides two-state onto-p-morphism counts for all finite rooted trees and m-middle fans: the present root-state method is not asserted to be new, and its recurrence may be derived from that more general enumeration by summing non-surjective classes. The cited 2011 modal notes and 2013 PlanetMath article give definitions and modal invariance rather than extremal counts. Zhang et al. (2012) optimize connected-subtree counts for trees, a strictly different invariant: rooted stars have exactly three p-morphisms but exponentially many center-containing subtrees. Semantic literature and primary-source queries checked precise target, aliases, the recurrence, different map-surjectivity conventions, and possible broader extremal tree results. No exact or stronger implication to the fixed-order optimizer was identified; unindexed coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: The total-map root recursion is algebraically recoverable from earlier onto-map methods; originality relies on the sharp fixed-order optimization and equality cases rather than on having a tree dynamic program.
No exhaustive search can rule out unindexed special extremal-tree results or a more general existing tree-product inequality.
The primary source on extremal connected-subtree counts differs as a statistic; similarity of shapes should not be mistaken for coverage.

value.rationale: For the basic branching Boolean-diamond S4 frame, exact bounded-morphism counts measure the multiplicity of modal behavior-preserving maps from finite rooted tree frames. The natural problem of maximizing this count subject only to a vertex budget has a full, all-size, unique structural solution, with an unexpected parity effect and exponential growth base sqrt(3). The minimizing rooted star and maximizing one- or two-level subdivided stars show that concentrating branching at the root is not enough: moving each leaf one level deeper changes the map count from constant three to exponential. This is not just a finite table or an arbitrary slice: it gives both extremal values and complete equality cases across all n, beyond the previously known least source size for a surjective map.
